automatedChecks.rule: Four distinct choices, exactly one of them the key, and the key is among them
No explanation names an answer by its position or letter
Every cited Alberta outcome resolves, and none is one the mapping calls not_measurable
Twenty-four objects in the roles a lesson expects; a worked example can never be answered
Nothing is released, and no item carries a status a parent did not grant
Explanations sit at or below the reading level of the lesson they belong to

findings.found: The correct answer appeared twice among the four choices, as "sand" and "sand — s-a-n-d", so the question could not be got wrong.
findings.action: Rewritten with four distinct choices before the content was committed.
findings.foundBy: writing the test that requires four distinct choices

findings.found: Two questions framed their choices inconsistently — one carried a sentence on two options and not the other two, which gave the answer away; the other read as a sentence about shortening rather than as a word.
findings.action: Both reframed before the content was committed.
findings.foundBy: reading the generated choices back

findings.found: draftedIn and skillIds were hand-written cross-references and were stale within a day: 9 outcomes reported as drafted when 16 had content, and 15 pack-to-mapping disagreements about which skill measures what.
findings.action: Both derived from the packs, as a union so no hand-made judgement is overwritten.
findings.foundBy: a cross-reference of every pack citation against the mapping

findings.found: The answer key cycled a, c, b, d over and over, so a child who noticed the pattern could answer without reading. The spread per position was even, which is why the balance rule alone did not catch it.
findings.action: Key positions re-placed in a sequence with no repeating cycle before the content was committed.
findings.foundBy: printing the key sequence of every pack

findings.found: Draft sound-counting items used whip and church. Some speakers say wh as two sounds, and programs disagree on whether ur is one sound or two, so neither word has a count everyone would accept.
findings.action: Replaced with thin and chick. The pack now avoids r-controlled vowels, x, qu, wh and n before k (as in drink, where programs disagree) wherever a count is asked. The digraph ng, as in sing, is kept and counted as one sound, as the rule states.
findings.foundBy: counting every keyed answer by hand against the rule the pack states

findings.found: Draft chunking items used magnetic and problem. Mag-ne-tic and pro-blem are both defensible splits, so a child could be marked wrong for a reasonable answer.
findings.action: Replaced with invented and picnic, whose splits are not in dispute.
findings.foundBy: trying the other syllable rules on each keyed split

findings.found: One explanation said that taking un away from uncle, under and unit leaves no base word, which is false for unit. A draft placement note gave a date for the second child’s diagnostic that nothing in the repository records.
findings.action: The explanation now says the u and n there do not mean not. The date was removed; the note says only that both children answered it.
findings.foundBy: reading every explanation and note back as a claim to be checked
